title: Light Conversion Control in NIR-Emissive Optical Materials Based on Heterolanthanide ErxYb3-x Quinolinolato Molecular Components

synthesis.procedure: A few drops of 28% aqueous NH3 were added to a suspension of 8-hydroxyquinoline (0.145 g, 1 mmol) in water (100 mL) under stirring to a final NH3 concentration of 2.0 × 10^-2 mol dm^-3 (pH ≈ 10). After 30 min, an aqueous solution of YbCl3·6H2O (0.129 g, 0.33 mmol) was added. The mixture was allowed to react for 2 days until unreacted white ligand disappeared. A yellow precipitate was collected by filtration, washed with water, 0.1 M NaOH, and water, and dried in an oven at 60 °C overnight (almost quantitative yield). The solid was dissolved in warm CH3CN, the solvent was rotary-evaporated to incipient precipitation, and yellow microcrystals of 1 formed after several days.
synthesis.temperature: ligand deprotonation at ambient conditions; drying at 60 °C; recrystallization from warm CH3CN
synthesis.time: 30 min after NH3 addition, then 2 days reaction; dried overnight; crystals after several days
synthesis.vessel_or_method: one-pot aqueous precipitation followed by CH3CN recrystallization
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtration; wash with water, 0.1 M NaOH, and water; oven-dry at 60 °C; dissolve in warm CH3CN and rotary-evaporate to incipient precipitation to give yellow microcrystals

properties.summary: Homoleptic Yb3Q9 shows ligand-centered visible photophysics and NIR Yb3+ 2F5/2 → 2F7/2 emission near 977–980 nm after ligand excitation. Ligand-to-Yb sensitization via the quinolinolate triplet is highly efficient (triplet lifetimes ~100–150 ps). In DMSO, Yb luminescence lifetimes of 1 and 1b are similar; in the crystalline solid, τYb(1) = 10.10 μs at 980 nm.

synthesis.procedure: Prepared analogously to 1: 8-hydroxyquinoline (0.145 g, 1 mmol) in water (100 mL) was deprotonated with 28% NH3 to 2.0 × 10^-2 mol dm^-3 (pH ≈ 10). After 30 min, aqueous Yb(NO3)3·6H2O (0.154 g, 0.33 mmol) was added and the mixture reacted for 2 days. The yellow precipitate was filtered, washed with water, 0.1 M NaOH, and water, and dried at 60 °C overnight (almost quantitative). Recrystallization from warm CH3CN gave yellow crystals of 1b; a colorless needle (0.011 × 0.019 × 0.099 mm3) was used for single-crystal XRD (CCDC 1054887).

properties.summary: 1b retains efficient ligand-to-Yb sensitization and NIR Yb emission near 977–980 nm. In DMSO, Yb lifetimes of 1 and 1b are similar despite nitrate substitution. In the solid state, τYb(1b) = 11.29 μs at 980 nm, longer than 1 (10.10 μs), attributed to fewer CH quenchers around Yb after replacing one Q by NO3-.

synthesis.procedure: Same aqueous one-pot procedure as 1: 1 mmol deprotonated 8-hydroxyquinoline treated with a mixture of 0.22 mmol YbCl3·6H2O and 0.11 mmol ErCl3·6H2O in water. Yellow precipitate collected, washed with water, 0.1 M NaOH, and water, dried at 60 °C overnight (yield >95%), and recrystallized from CH3CN to yellow microcrystals. The product was also obtained from two equivalents of Er3+ chloride plus one equivalent of Yb3+ acetate or triflate (text notes this for the Er-rich analogue pathway; for 2 the chloride mixture above is the stated recipe).
synthesis.time: procedure as for 1 (2 days); dried overnight
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtration, aqueous/NaOH washes, oven dry, recrystallization from CH3CN

properties.summary: Mixed Er/Yb species 2 shows dual NIR luminescence at ~1 μm (Yb) and ~1.5 μm (Er) after ligand excitation, with quantitative Yb-to-Er RET favored by short intermetallic distances. Ligand-to-metal sensitization remains highly efficient. GLYMO silica films doped with 2 retain solution-like dual NIR emission and RET dynamics (Yb 980 nm: 1.48 μs 60% and 6.57 μs 40%; Er 1540 nm: 0.41 μs 60% and 1.81 μs 40%; λexc 355 nm).

properties.summary: Er-rich homoleptic 3 shows dual NIR Yb/Er luminescence after ligand excitation. Yb-to-Er RET is quantitative and 1540 nm intensity is largely independent of the number of Er ions across the mixed series. Powder XRD confirmed isostructurality of 1 and 3 with previously reported 2.
